A1.justification: Both PDFs describe 3DGS-HPC. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on RobustNeRF, On-the-go, and Phototourism, along with ablations, sensitivity studies, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and adds mask-boundary and dominant-distractor experiments in Appendix B.3–B.4.

M1.justification: Patch aggregation, photometric GMM classification, perceptual percentile thresholding, mask intersection, and masked 3DGS optimization remain unchanged. The appearance-embedding extension was already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RobustNeRF, On-the-go, and Phototourism scenes. v2 adds a distinct synthetic stress scenario with colored patches occluding more than 50% of every RobustNeRF training image (Appendix B.4), extending input conditions without adding another dataset.

E2.justification: RobustSplat is added to both main benchmark comparisons in Figures 6–7. The new stress test also includes 3DGS with ground-truth masks as an upper-bound comparator. Existing comparator sets, including Phototourism's, are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: New protocols compare unchanged ground-truth masks, five-pixel dilation, conversion to 16×16 patches, and 10% patch misclassification, and test synthetic majority occlusion with a ground-truth-mask control. Existing benchmark resolutions, metrics, and default hyperparameters remain unchanged; no corresponding protocol revision explains the changed Phototourism scores.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 and Table 4 newly isolate boundary imprecision from region misclassification; B.4 and Table 5 test GMM classification under dominant distractors, including assignment accuracy. These substantially extend direct validation of two central assumptions. The patch-size and warm-up studies already existed in v1 and are merely moved into Section 5.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The new tables continue point-estimate reporting, and the retained sensitivity plots do not introduce uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 13 revises most Phototourism entries: Ours with embeddings changes average PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS from 24.31/.863/.132 to 23.19/.867/.120, while NeRF-HuGS PSNR changes from 22.80 to 24.27, reversing their PSNR ordering. These are revised reports, not established algorithmic gains or losses. v2 also adds RobustSplat results and Tables 4–5; the stress test reports PSNR 24.85 for Ours versus 15.93 for 3DGS. Existing numerical entries in Figures 6–9 are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and classification equations are unchanged. v1's separate photometric and perceptual error equations are combined under one equation number in v2. The new GMM discussion supplies an empirical interpretation, not a formal theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: patch-wise classification and a hybrid photometric/perceptual metric for robust distractor-free reconstruction. v2 clarifies the distinction between semantic grouping and perceptual features without introducing a different central contribution or task scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a multi-view explanation for tolerating coarse mask boundaries, and B.4 argues that GMM component identity remains stable despite dominant distractors. Appendix C newly identifies microscopic objects and thin static structures as potential patch-wise failure cases, supplementing the retained visibility and unseen-content limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and explicitly states that the main comparisons use default settings without per-scene tuning. It also identifies manual ground-truth annotations and perturbation parameters for the new tests. Existing hardware, feature-layer selections, and mask-update details remain unchanged; the link alone does not establish code or data availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds RobustSplat to the cited semantic-prior literature and removes the SuGAR and Scaffold-GS references. The broader research positioning is retained. Publication updates for existing references and the switch to author-year citations do not represent additional works.

P1.justification: v2 refines the abstract and semantic-prior explanations, moves the hyperparameter discussion into the main ablation section, and reorganizes supplementary sections as Appendices A–D. It also adds acknowledgements, an impact statement, and affiliation details. Most substantive prose and the main narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different publication template, expands Figures 6–7 with comparator rows, and adds Tables 4–5. The sensitivity figures move from the appendix into the main text, with corresponding renumbering. Figure 13 replaces one qualitative rendering; most other visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new boundary and majority-occlusion tests provide direct evidence for assumptions previously supported mainly by explanation or citations. RobustSplat comparisons and explicit thin-structure limitations also improve evaluation and qualification. These are useful but bounded gains: Appendix B.4's categorical GMM claims exceed what its stress test establishes, and the unexplained Phototourism revisions cannot themselves be treated as improved performance or reliability.
